evidence.claim: The South Carolina Department of Transportation describes a 22-mile route with landscaped medians and broad views, where local limits on signs, setbacks and density have moderated commercial development.
evidence.quote: Commercial development has mushroomed in recent years, but local ordinances have limited the impact by requiring set-backs, sign sizes/locations, and density limits.

evidence.claim: Between the mainland and Hilton Head, Pinckney Island National Wildlife Refuge includes salt marsh, tidal creeks, forest and freshwater ponds.
evidence.quote: Nearly 67% of the refuge consists of salt marsh and tidal creeks.  A wide variety of land types are found on Pinckney Island alone:  saltmarsh, forestland, brushland, fallow field and freshwater ponds.

evidence.quote: The James F. Byrnes Bridge was built in 1956. It was a two-lane toll swing bridge constructed at a cost of $1.5 million that opened the island to automobile traffic from the mainland.
